name: The tail pin and Tail Torque Assist follow the tail mode on save
step: Check MSP2_TAIL_MOTOR_OUTPUT and the TTA writes
rationale:
Many boards come with the tail pin on SERVO 4, so a motorised tail had no MOTOR 2
and never ran. rotorflight-firmware's MSP2_TAIL_MOTOR_OUTPUT (0x5F14, API 12.10)
moves the pin between SERVO 4 and MOTOR 2, and the Mixer -> Tail page now sends it on
save through lib/msp_tail_motor_output.lua. A change between a servo and a motor tail
also writes Tail Torque Assist (gain 100 or 0) on every PID profile.

The harness drives the real module with the real bus and the real status, profile
select and governor profile codecs, and answers every request as the firmware would.
It pins the request payloads (action 0, 1 or 2), that an FC without the command and a
short reply both read as unsupported instead of failing the page, that a refused move
keeps the save going with its reason recorded, that BOTH and NONE are left alone, and
that TTA is written on each profile where it differs before the active profile is
selected again.

--self-test re-runs the move checks against a copy of the module that never asks for a
move, and requires them to fail.
